long_biography.plain_text:
Physics led Jonathan Faiman into markets rather than research. After graduating from Imperial College London, he traded at Bankers Trust and later headed emerging-market trading at Goldman Sachs. In 2000, he joined two Goldman colleagues to found Ocado. Its model paired online grocery ordering with a purpose-built central fulfilment operation, and Faiman served as chief operating officer while the business scaled.

Faiman left Ocado before its flotation and sold most of his remaining founder shares during the listing. He subsequently returned to building and investing in technology-led platforms. At Anoto, he first led commercial operations and the team behind its inq product portfolio before becoming chief executive in March 2026. His present remit centres on digital writing, software and AI-enabled workflows; it is a current operating role, distinct from the Ocado stake that generated his documented exit proceeds.
